title: Public vs internal model metadata + release note redaction rules (enforcement, checklist, tests)
creator: Naomi Feldman
project: Model metadata schema v1 + automated changelog generator
description:
We are standardizing model/version metadata (schema v1) and generating customer-visible release notes from model metadata + change events. This introduces a high-risk class of issues: leaking internal-only details (e.g., incident references, customer names, vendor identifiers, internal eval artifacts, or security-sensitive remediation notes) into the public release notes feed (Console + docs + SDK endpoints).

This ticket defines the redaction rules and enforces them at generation time and at read time (RBAC), with a review checklist and automated test coverage.

Motivating incidents/near-misses:
- Console rollout UI briefly showed internal notes to non-admins (later hotfixed; see PR-18463).
- Docs build published an incomplete/incorrect note during a generator failure mode (see #incidents thread 1743604432).
- Support tickets requesting exact model change history while ensuring we don’t expose internal context in public feeds (SUP-28429).

Non-goals:
- Full end-user notification subscriptions (email/webhook) beyond internal plumbing.
- Rewriting all historical release notes (only minimal backfill).
proposal_summary: Introduce an explicit visibility model for all human-authored fields used in changelog/release-note generation: public | restricted | internal. Enforce redaction in the generator pipeline (artifact creation), and also enforce at API/Console render time via RBAC. Provide deterministic unit tests and e2e tests to prevent regressions.
redaction_policy_v1:
Definitions:
- public: safe for customer-visible surfaces (Console release notes, docs site, public SDK endpoints).
- restricted: safe only for authenticated customer admins of the tenant/workspace (Console only), not for docs site; used sparingly for operationally useful detail (e.g., “roll back guidance”, “workaround”, additional compatibility detail) that isn’t sensitive but could be confusing at a broad public level.
- internal: Redwood employees only (internal admin tools, audit views), never on customer-visible surfaces.

Rule 1: Default deny
- Any freeform text field without an explicit visibility marker MUST be treated as internal.
- Generator must fail closed if it cannot determine visibility.

Rule 2: Explicit field allowlist for public
Only the following fields may be emitted into public release-note artifacts:
- title (public)
- summary (public)
- categories (public, from taxonomy)
- severity (public, from taxonomy)
- effective_date (public)
- affected_deployments (public)
- availability (public; deployment/region matrix limited to non-sensitive granularity)
- compatibility (public; model family compatibility, API behavior compatibility; must not include customer-specific routing rules)
- deprecation (public; timeline and impact language per style guide)
- rollback_guidance (restricted/public depending on content)
- links (public; only to docs URLs or generic guidance; no internal links)

Rule 3: Explicit forbidden content patterns (hard block)
If any public or restricted field contains:
- references to internal systems (e.g., linear keys ENG-/PM-/DES-, Jira INT- keys, internal Slack links, internal Confluence URLs)
- incident identifiers or postmortem links
- customer names, domains, or account IDs (unless explicitly approved and part of a customer-specific restricted note, which is out of scope for MVP)
- security vulnerability identifiers prior to public disclosure (CVE references allowed only after Security signs off; otherwise internal)
- infrastructure/provider identifiers that reveal sensitive topology (exact GPU hostnames, IPs, AZ identifiers, internal cluster names)
- credentials/secrets/tokens (obvious)
Then:
- public artifact generation MUST fail (CI + generator runtime), and log a structured internal error with redacted preview.

Rule 4: Soft redaction (sanitize) for restricted/internal
For restricted/internal artifacts, we allow internal references but they must not be rendered to public. Additionally, internal artifacts should replace secrets-like patterns with [REDACTED] even internally (defense in depth) and emit an audit event.

Rule 5: Links policy
- public/restricted links must match an allowlist of domains: docs.redwoodinference.com, console.redwoodinference.com/help, status.redwoodinference.com.
- internal links allowed only in internal visibility.
- If a link is disallowed, treat the field as internal or fail generation (configurable; MVP: fail for public, downgrade to internal for restricted).

Rule 6: Audience consistency across surfaces
- Anything that appears in docs site is public.
- Console release notes default to public, with an explicit toggle to view restricted (customer admin only) if present.
- Internal admin surfaces can view all three visibilities.

Rule 7: Auditability
- Every redaction or visibility downgrade must emit an audit event (ties to ENG-9828) containing: model_id, version, field_path, old_visibility, new_visibility, reason_code (pattern_match / domain_not_allowed / missing_visibility / unknown_field), actor (service), and trace_id.

Rule 8: Templating restrictions
- Templates must not interpolate internal fields into public variants. Templates should be split by audience rather than branching on if statements inside a single template (reduces footguns).

Rule 9: “Public summary” must be independently authored
- If internal notes exist, they must not be auto-summarized into public text. Public summary must be explicitly provided by the author or derived from safe structured fields (categories/severity/compat).
implementation_plan:
1) Schema-level changes (if needed)
- Add visibility markers to relevant metadata fields used by generator (or confirm existing public/internal split from ADR-0142). For MVP, implement at changelog entry level (the release-note payload) even if the underlying model metadata has more granular visibilities.

2) Generator enforcement (ENG-9823)
- Add a redaction module used by both event->artifact generation and preview generation in CI.
- Implement allowlist-based serialization for public artifacts.
- Add forbidden-pattern scanning for public + restricted fields (regex + heuristics).
- Implement link allowlist validator.
- Failure mode: if public artifact cannot be generated safely, generator emits only internal artifact and marks public artifact as blocked, with a reason and a remediation hint.

3) API/Console enforcement (ENG-9824)
- Backend endpoints must filter by viewer role:
  - public feed: only public visibility
  - console customer-admin: public + restricted
  - internal admin: all
- Ensure server-side filtering; UI must not rely on client filtering.

4) CI enforcement (ENG-9826)
- Add required checks: release note preview must include visibility annotations and must pass forbidden-pattern scan.
- PR fails if:
  - public fields include forbidden patterns
  - any new freeform note field lacks visibility
  - disallowed links present in public/restricted

5) Documentation + review checklist
- Add “Release notes safety checklist” to the style guide and the release process playbook, including examples of what NOT to include.

6) Backfill/fixtures
- Add fixtures covering:
  - safe public change
  - restricted change with workaround
  - internal-only change referencing incident
  - broken change with internal link in public field (must fail)

acceptance_criteria:
1) Generator produces three deterministic artifacts from the same event stream: public, restricted, internal (restricted optional).
2) Public artifact never includes internal-only fields; verified by unit tests and an e2e test.
3) Forbidden content patterns cause a hard failure for public artifact generation and block publishing (CI + runtime).
4) Console endpoints enforce server-side RBAC filtering; a non-admin cannot retrieve restricted/internal data via API.
5) Every redaction/downgrade emits an audit event with reason_code.
6) “Default deny” behavior is implemented: any unrecognized field or missing visibility is internal.
7) A documented checklist exists and is linked from the PR template / release process notes.
8) Regression test added for the prior leak class (internal notes rendering to non-admin).
review_checklist:
Author checklist (required when touching model metadata or release note templates):
- [ ] All human-authored text fields have explicit visibility (public/restricted/internal).
- [ ] Public summary contains no internal identifiers (tickets, incidents, Slack, internal URLs).
- [ ] Public links only point to docs/help/status domains.
- [ ] No customer names/domains/account IDs present.
- [ ] No security vulnerability details unless explicitly cleared for public disclosure.
- [ ] Language follows taxonomy/style guide (no overclaiming perf/quality; includes caveats).
- [ ] Rollback guidance present when change is breaking or medium/high risk.

Reviewer checklist (Eng + Security):
- [ ] CI release-note preview artifact reviewed in PR.
- [ ] Any restricted content is truly necessary and safe for customer-admin.
- [ ] Redaction audit events validated in staging logs.
- [ ] E2E test coverage includes: non-admin view, customer-admin view, internal-admin view.
- [ ] Confirm docs build consumes only public artifacts.
test_plan:
Unit tests:
- test_default_deny_unknown_field_is_internal
- test_public_allowlist_serialization_drops_internal_fields
- test_forbidden_pattern_blocks_public_generation (Linear/Jira keys, internal URLs)
- test_link_allowlist_enforced
- test_downgrade_restricted_to_internal_when_link_disallowed
- test_audit_event_emitted_on_redaction

Integration tests:
- generator -> artifact storage: public artifact blocked state persisted and surfaced
- console API: viewer role matrix returns correct visibilities

E2E (QA automation; see e2e test plan doc):
- Scenario A: metadata edit with internal note; verify non-admin cannot see it; customer-admin cannot see it unless marked restricted.
- Scenario B: attempt to include internal Confluence link in public summary; verify CI fails and generator blocks publish.
- Scenario C: docs build consumes artifact and publishes page; verify restricted/internal entries absent.

Security tests:
- Negative test: craft request to change-history endpoint with query params attempting to request internal visibility; verify server ignores/denies.
- Snapshot test: ensure responses never contain internal fields for non-admin roles.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): enable redaction enforcement in warn-only mode for restricted/internal; hard-fail for public. Collect metrics on blocked publishes.
Phase 2 (prod, 10%): enforce hard-fail for public; continue warn-only for restricted downgrade.
Phase 3 (prod, 100%): full enforcement; require checklist link in PR template; support playbook updated.
Rollback: feature-flag redaction module; in emergency, disable public publishing but keep internal artifact generation + audit events.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-blocking causes release note publish delays.
Mitigation: clear failure reasons + remediation guidance; allow restricted/internal generation even when public is blocked.

Risk: A new field added to schema bypasses redaction.
Mitigation: allowlist-only serialization for public; default deny for unknown fields; CI test that enumerates supported fields.

Risk: UI bug re-renders internal data.
Mitigation: server-side filtering + contract tests; add regression test for the class of bug fixed in PR-18463.

Risk: Private deployments require different packaging.
Mitigation: ensure export pipeline uses public artifacts by default; allow an “enterprise bundle” artifact that is restricted-only when contractually permitted (later; out of MVP).

progress_updates: 2025-10-10 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted v1 policy (default deny + allowlist). Shared with Marcus Lin + Naomi Feldman for review. Open question: do we need ‘restricted’ in MVP or can we ship public/internal only? PM preference is to include restricted for rollback/workaround details in Console only.

2025-10-14 (Marcus Lin): Security review: strong preference for allowlist-only serialization for public. Add explicit forbidden patterns: internal Confluence, Slack permalinks, Linear/Jira keys, incident IDs. Also require link allowlist. Requested audit event emission on any downgrade/redaction.
2025-10-18 (Marissa Cole): PM sign-off on including ‘restricted’ tier, but must keep it rare and use only for tenant-admin surfaces. Docs must remain strictly public.

2025-10-22 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented redaction module in generator + added unit tests. Wired into CI preview step behind flag. Added contract test for Console endpoint role filtering. Pending: finalize reviewer checklist wording with Docs (Wei) and ensure audit events are emitted (blocked on ENG-9828 merge).
comments: Jada Williams (2025-10-15): Please make sure we enforce on the backend API. We’ve been burned by client-side filtering assumptions. Also: consider pagination edge cases where mixed-visibility notes could cause count/next-page token mismatch if filtering happens after pagination.

Connor O'Brien (2025-10-16): For CI: we need a stable artifact that reviewers can see in PR checks. Suggest uploading both public preview and internal preview, but ensure internal preview is only visible to employees (GitHub permissions). At minimum, public preview must be mandatory.

Wei Chen (2025-10-17): Style guide alignment: public notes should never mention internal eval run IDs; we can say “Quality regression checks passed” only if backed by structured fields. Also avoid % improvements unless we can cite methodology; otherwise use “reduced latency in common prompts” language.

Svetlana Petrenko (2025-10-21): Audit events should include reason_code and field_path; please avoid including full original text in the audit payload. We can store a hash + truncated sample if necessary for debugging.

Leila Farouk (2025-10-23): Add one e2e case specifically for the prior leak: internal note present + non-admin user opens rollout panel. Assert DOM doesn’t contain internal text and network response doesn’t contain internal fields.
open_questions: Should restricted visibility be allowed in SDK endpoints for authenticated customer admins, or Console-only for MVP? (current proposal: Console-only)
Do we need locale/i18n considerations in redaction scans (non-English content)? (MVP: regex-based scanning; revisit later)
How to handle vendor advisories (e.g., CUDA driver fixes) that might be sensitive but important? (proposal: restricted with Security approval)
